main.t: The single bone of the forehead, which also forms the roof of each orbit (frontal bone).

simpler.t: The frontal bone is your forehead bone.

deeper.t: Inside the skull, it forms most of the floor of the anterior cranial fossa.

facts.t: It forms the forehead, at the front of the brain case.
Behind, it meets the two parietal bones at the coronal suture.
Below, it forms the upper margin and the roof of each orbit.

simpler.t: It forms your forehead and the top of your eye sockets.

deeper.t: It is one of the eight brain case bones, and one of four that meet at the pterion.

items.name: Glabella
items.t: A slight hollow between the eyebrows, at the front midline.

items.name: Supraorbital margin
items.t: The upper rim of each orbit.

items.name: Supraorbital foramen
items.t: An opening near the middle of each margin, for a sensory nerve to the forehead.

items.name: Brow ridges
items.t: Rounded thickenings just above each margin, behind the eyebrows.

items.name: Orbital part
items.t: A flat region that forms the roof of the orbits and the floor of the anterior cranial fossa.

items.name: Frontal sinus
items.t: An air-filled space just above the eyebrows: the most anterior paranasal sinus.

simpler.t: It has a curved front, rims over the eyes and a flat part extending back inside the skull.

deeper.t: The frontal sinus may be one space, or divided at the midline into left and right.

facts.t: Its curved front encloses the frontal lobes of the brain, which lie in the anterior cranial fossa.
The thickened rims of the orbits help protect the eyes.
Its sinus lightens the skull and adds resonance to the voice.

simpler.t: It shields the front of the brain and the tops of the eyes.

items.name: Coronal suture
items.t: Joins it to the right and left parietal bones, across the top of the skull.

items.name: Pterion
items.t: Where the frontal, parietal, temporal and sphenoid bones meet: the weakest part of the skull.

items.name: Frontal lobes
items.t: Lie in the anterior cranial fossa, which the frontal bone mostly floors.

items.name: Ethmoid bone
items.t: Its crista galli and cribriform plates lie in the midline of the same floor.

items.name: Orbit
items.t: The frontal bone forms its roof.

simpler.t: It joins the parietal bones behind and roofs the eye sockets below.

facts.t: Like the other bones of the top and sides of the brain case, it forms directly from membrane (intramembranous ossification).
At birth, it is in two halves, which fuse in early childhood.
The anterior fontanelle, the soft spot at the front of a baby’s head, lies where it meets the parietal bones.
The brow ridges vary in size and are generally larger in males.
The frontal sinus may be a single space or two.

items.damaged: The lining of the frontal sinus swells and blocks its narrow passage to the nasal cavity.
items.cannotDo: Be free of pressure and pain above the eyebrows.
items.why: The blocked sinus fills with fluid, and the pressure causes pain.

items.injury: A strong blow to the forehead.
items.damaged: The bone breaks; in a depressed fracture, it is pushed inwards.
items.cannotDo: Escape the risk of bleeding inside the skull, which can injure the brain.
items.why: The frontal lobes lie directly behind the bone.

items.q: Explain how the frontal bone takes part in both the orbit and the cranial cavity.
model: Its front forms the forehead and the supraorbital margins.
Inside the skull it extends backwards as a flat region.
This region forms the roof of the orbits below.
And it forms most of the floor of the anterior cranial fossa above.

items.q: Compare the frontal bone with the parietal bones.
model: The frontal bone is single and forms the forehead.
The parietal bones are paired and form most of the upper sides of the skull.
They meet at the coronal suture.
All of them form directly from membrane.

items.q: Predict where a patient with a blocked frontal sinus feels pain, and explain why.
model: Just above the eyebrows, where the frontal sinus lies.
Swollen lining blocks the narrow passage to the nasal cavity.

check.stem: Which suture joins the frontal bone to the parietal bones?
check.why: The coronal suture runs across the skull between them.

options: The opening for the nerve to the forehead
check.why: The glabella is the slight depression at the front midline, between the eyebrows.

check.stem: Which part of the brain lies behind the frontal bone, in the anterior cranial fossa?
check.why: The anterior cranial fossa contains the frontal lobes.
